naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to create a permanent outdoor farmers market. The goal is to demolish two buildings that have been deemed unsafe by a structural engineer and create a permanent space for local craft and produce vendors to sell their items. The space will be enhanced with a pergola over the green space, electricity, and triangle shades over the area to protect the shoppers and vendors from the elements of the weather. The site for the outdoor market is in a prime location of downtown called Hebron and is accessible to all ages, income levels, and is easily accessed from Highway 81. By constructing a permanent space, Hebron will be able to host several community events throughout the spring, summer and fall seasons and encourage a wide variety of small businesses (e.g. food trucks, produce vendors, local crafters) across Thayer County to promote and sell goods and services within downtown Hebron. This could, in turn, increase long-term investment in Hebron downtown and generate additional sales tax for the community. The market would complement county-wide business retention by showcasing local goods and services while also encouraging job creation by providing an extra venue to host events that increase part-time and seasonal employment opportunities. This project is expected to assist at a minimum of 4 small and emerging businesses and create or support 7.5 full-time equivalent jobs in the next 3 years.

This will allow the college to offer a full welding program and complement their current construction program. Rural Development funded the construction of the welding shop with RBDG funding in 2020. Both the Omaha and Santee Reservations suffer from multiple challenges including poverty, a struggling economy, and a serious lack of economic development. Growing the vocational training opportunities at NICC via the addition of welding training will provide entrepreneurs with a useful trade skill, which is high demand in the area. This project is expected to assist at a minimum of 2 small and emerging business and will create at least 4 full-time equivalent jobs in the next three years.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will cover a cost overrun for a sewer improvement project that will upgrade the existing collection system and construct new lagoons required to meet applicable health and sanitary standards, specifically the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) limits. The effluent from the villages one cell-controlled discharge lagoon is not able to meet the present permit levels making the village in violation of the Clean Water Act NPDES permit. The village is also having infiltration and inflow issues with the collection system, which results in high inaccurate wastewater flows for the village, causing more wear and tear on the system. The suggested improvements are to construct a new 3-cell lagoon system with a controlled discharge via land application, a combination of replacement and relining of the collection system, and the installation of new water meters. The existing lift station will be updated. The new lagoon system will put them back in compliance with the NPDES permit, and the collection system improvements and water meter installation will reduce the amount of infiltration and inaccurate readings of wastewater flows.

funding_code: (LOAN ONLY) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to improve and update the villages water system required to meet applicable health and sanitary standards. The villages water system consists of two wells developed in 1978 and 1987 along with the existing standpipe thought to be 40 plus years old. The villages problem with the water system are the existing wells, which the Department of Health and Human Services identified uranium levels above safe drinking water standards. Village leadership has addressed the problem with this funding request to drill a new well, develop and construct a blending station and add a generator for backup power during emergencies. The two existing wells will also be refurbished and a new stainless-steel standpipe will be constructed to replace the existing one. The blending station will include controls to blend water from all three wells to mitigate the uranium concern and return the community water standards back to a safe source of drinking water. This project will benefit the Villages 94 residents and 47 users.

project_announced_description: Rural Development funds will be used to connect the Village of Bristow to the existing Boyd County Rural Water District No. 2s six-inch water main. A transmission main will be added to existing Rural Water Districts water main and extend to the south end of the business district in the Village, ending with a meter pit. The existing water tank level will also be modified with a pressure reducing valve to control the water flow helping to correct water issues for the Village, including a boil order that was issued for a time last summer because of E-Coli contaminant in the water. Although the boil order has been lifted, there is still a level of concern. Additionally, the Department of Health and Human Services has come to the conclusion that one of the Villages wells is under the direct influence of surface water due to root invasion and a persistent presence of E-Coli. This project will allow Bristow to hook on to the Rural Water District and remedy all health and pressure concerns.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide training and technical assistance in the cities of Columbus, Norfolk, Hastings, and Nebraska City for small and emerging food businesses. Training will assist Latinos with developing home-based food businesses or starting new business enterprises in their community. Workshops and trainings will be facilitated in both English and Spanish to ensure wider access to information. Participants will receive training in completing a business plan and food-handling permit requirements, as well as information on local opportunities for business space. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide training and technical assistance in Thurston, Burt, and Knox counties for small food and art-based businesses located on the Omaha and Santee Reservations. The project will provide training workshops focusing on entrepreneurship opportunities for tribal businesses in the realms of horticulture, flavored teas, and honey production. The project will focus on small and emerging businesses located in Burt and Knox counties as well as Thurston county, NE, which is classified as a persistent poverty county.
